Looking at the validator output, the issue is clear: in genre `block`, the keyword for declaring a component isn't `block` (that word is already spent naming the genre on line 1) — it's `node`. That also resolves the "unknown endpoint" errors, since those were only unknown because no node with that id had actually been declared (the `block ...` lines were rejected before they could register the ids).

```fd
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Telemetry export pipeline"

node poller "Poller"
node normalizer "Normalizer"
node healthprobe "Health probe"
node buffer "Ring buffer"
node exporter "Exporter"

edge poller -> normalizer
edge healthprobe -> normalizer
edge normalizer -> buffer
edge buffer -> exporter
```

This captures exactly what the description states: two independent sources (`poller`, `healthprobe`) feeding `normalizer`, which feeds `buffer`, which feeds `exporter` — no more, no less. I didn't add labels to the edges since the prose already carries that detail (poller is timer-driven, health probe pings independently, buffer holds briefly) and the figure's job here is just the topology.
